response:
Diagnosis: the design space is now well mapped. Two axes matter — how many investment legs, and which intangible conditioner. Adding the second capex denominator raised the slope (FMB -5.72) but slightly diluted alpha; switching the conditioner to value added per worker (gross profit per employee) produced the archive's most reliable alpha (Dual_Peak_Capex_Low_Value_Added_Per_Worker: alpha -5.1%, t=-5.49) while trimming the slope to -4.87. The single-denominator, productivity-conditioned signal (Abnormal_Capacity_Buildup_Unproductive: FMB -5.38, alpha -5.4%, t=-5.22, Sharpe -0.519) still dominates on the joint criterion, which means the untested cell — one capex denominator with the value-added conditioner — is the highest-value experiment left. Gen-7 also confirmed my vintage repair: taking the change in the undepreciated plant share turned a null alpha (t=-1.55) into a real one (-3.5%, t=-3.42) with FMB -4.76, so stock rejuvenation and flow peaks are complementary build measures worth fusing. The goodwill family remains the alpha maximum (-6.5% to -6.8%) and deserves the upgraded conditioner. Remaining slots go to an operator-structure test (continuous excess-over-own-norm instead of a rank), a long-side refinement, and one new financing channel.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Peak_Capex_Low_Value_Added_Per_Worker
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Physical capital spending at a five-year peak relative to installed plant, undertaken by firms whose value added per worker is low for their industry, is the cleanest statement of tangible overexpansion without intangible capital to support it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This fills the one untested cell of the archive's design grid: the single best-alpha investment leg paired with the best-alpha conditioner, both of which have been validated separately (alpha -5.4% with productivity; alpha t=-5.49 with value added per worker under two denominators). Parsimony matters here because each additional ranked leg has cost slope strength, so a two-leg version should retain the -5.4 FMB while capturing the value-added conditioner's alpha reliability at full coverage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Flow_And_Vintage_Build_Burst_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), DELTA(RATIO(ppent, ppegt), 1)), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is unambiguously in a build cycle when its spending flow is at a multi-year peak and its plant is simultaneously getting younger relative to gross cost; unproductive operators in this state have just sunk capital they cannot monetize.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The vintage-change leg is an independently validated build measure (FMB -4.76, alpha -3.5%, t=-3.42) built from balance-sheet stocks rather than the cash-flow statement, so it carries information the capex flow misses — for instance disposals of old plant alongside new construction. Fusing a flow measure with a stock measure of the same economic event should sharpen the short leg more than stacking two flow normalizations did in gen 6.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Goodwill_Overhang_Low_Value_Added
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(gdwl, sale), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: Acquired goodwill is impaired when the combined firm cannot generate value added per employee; goodwill-heavy firms with low gross profit per worker have demonstrably failed to realize the synergies they paid for.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The goodwill family holds the archive's largest alphas, and its slope responded only to productivity conditioning (from 0.05 to -2.4, then -2.9 with the dual moat), so replacing the two separate moat legs with the single value-added-per-worker measure that fuses margin and efficiency should raise the gradient without diluting the -6.8% alpha. Keeping the signal to two legs also stabilizes portfolio composition in the coverage-constrained goodwill subsample.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Capex_Above_Own_Norm_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(RATIO(capx, ppent), MA(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp))))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically meaningful quantity is how far current investment intensity exceeds the firm's own five-year norm in proportional terms, not merely its ordinal position within that history.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates an operator-structure choice against the front-runner: a continuous excess-over-own-average ratio instead of TS_RANK, which compresses a firm doubling its normal spending and a firm exceeding it by 5% into the same top rank. If the continuous version improves the slope and the extreme-decile alpha, the mechanism is about the magnitude of the investment shock and the final signal should adopt it; if not, the ordinal state is the right representation and we learn the effect is threshold-like.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Sustained_Research_High_Value_Added_Restraint
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp)), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(xrd, 3), sale), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: The long side is best defined by a durable research commitment rather than a single year's R&D: firms with three years of cumulative research spending relative to revenue, high value added per worker, and capital spending below their own norm are compounding unrecognized intangible capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The value-added conditioner already lifted the long side to its best result (alpha +3.6%, t=3.56, Sharpe 0.174, FMB 2.36), and the remaining weakness is the noisy single-year R&D leg, which makes membership in the long portfolio unstable; a three-year cumulative research intensity is the natural stock analogue and should raise both the slope and the Sharpe. A credible long leg is necessary because every strong archive result to date is short-side driven.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Equity_Funded_Peak_Expansion_Unproductive
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5), SUMRANK(RATIO(sstk, at), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(sale, emp)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Overexpansion is most damaging when it must be funded by selling stock: unproductive firms that issue equity to finance a peak capital-spending cycle combine negative investment and negative financing information, and management is exploiting favorable pricing to fund poor projects.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Financing has been probed only in isolation — equity issuance as a negative modifier on R&D (gen 1) and debt on intangible collateral (gen 3, wrong sign) — but never as the funding source of the validated peak-capex state, so this tests whether the source of funds adds information beyond the investment state and the intangible deficit. It is the one distinct economic channel in this batch and it keeps near-full coverage since sstk is widely reported.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
